items.title: 11.2.1 Steps to Find the Domain of a Vector-Valued Function (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 288-289: 11.2.1 Step-1, Step-2, definition of range, printed Example 1 (shown as Example 3): domain and range of sqrt(4 - t^2) i + 1/(t - 1) j

blocks.text: Pichle page par humne parha ke domain mein woh \(t\) aate hain jin par har component defined ho. Ab kitab isi baat ko do saaf steps mein likhti hai, aur saath hi range ki definition bhi deti hai. Yeh page exam ke lehaaz se bohat aham hai, kyun ke domain aur range ke sawal aksar aate hain.
Step-1: Har component ka domain alag alag nikaaliye.
Step-2: Components \(f(t)\), \(g(t)\) aur \(h(t)\) ke domains ka intersection (common hissa) lijiye. \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka domain inhi domains ka intersection hai.
Range ki definition: vector-valued function ki range un tamam output vectors \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka set hai jo \(t\) ke domain mein badalne se bante hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Domain ka sawal hai: "kaun se \(t\) andar daal sakte hain?" Range ka sawal hai: "kaun se vectors bahar aate hain?"
Har output vector \(\langle x(t), y(t)\rangle\) origin se draw karein to ek point par khatam hota hai, is liye range asal mein us curve ke points ka set hai jo \(\mathbf{r}\) banata hai. Har component ki range alag nikaalne se sirf yeh pata chalta hai ke curve kis patti (strip) ya dabbe (box) mein hai; lekin un values ka har jora curve par nahin hota, kyun ke ek hi \(t\) sab components ko ek saath tay karta hai. Misal: ek train ka time-table, har station ka waqt train ke safar se jura hai; aap kisi bhi station ko kisi bhi waqt se nahin jor sakte.

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: Kitab yahan se examples ki ginti dobara 1 se shuru kar deti hai: yeh misaal kitab mein "Example 1" chhapi hai (pehle wale Example 1 aur 2 11.1.3 mein hain). Is portal par Unit 11 ki saari misaalen ek hi silsile mein ginti ki gayi hain, is liye yeh Example 3 hai. Kitab ka number → portal ka number: Example 1 → 3 (yeh), Example 2 → 4 aur Example 3 → 5 (dono 11.3.1 mein), Example 4 → 6 aur Example 5 → 7 (11.4), Example 6 → 8 aur Example 7 → 9 (11.5).

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem:
Find the domain and range of the vector-valued function
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{4 - t^{2}}\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}\hat{j}\]
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{4 - t^{2}}\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}\hat{j}\); components \(x(t) = \sqrt{4 - t^{2}}\) aur \(y(t) = \dfrac{1}{t - 1}\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}\) ka domain aur range.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle 11.2.1 ke do steps: har component ka domain alag, phir un ka common hissa (intersection). Us ke baad dekhenge ke domain wale \(t\) par kaun se output vectors bante hain; wahi range hai.

Step 1: Pehle component ka domain
\(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka domain woh tamam \(t\) hain jin par dono components defined hon. Pehla component \(\sqrt{4 - t^{2}}\) hai, aur square root ke andar wali cheez negative nahin ho sakti: \(4 - t^{2} \ge 0\).
\[\Rightarrow t^{2} \le 4\]
\[\Rightarrow -2 \le t \le 2\]
\[\Rightarrow t \in [-2, 2]\]
Kyun: negative number ka square root real number nahin hota. Dhyan dein: \(t^{2} \le 4\) se sirf \(t \le 2\) nahin, balke \(-2 \le t \le 2\) aata hai.

Step 2: Doosre component ka domain
\(\frac{1}{t-1}\) mein denominator zero nahin ho sakta:
\[t - 1 \ne 0 \Rightarrow t \ne 1\]
Kyun: zero se divide karna defined nahin.

Step 3: Domains ka intersection
Dono shartein ek saath poori honi chahiye, to final domain:
\[t \in [-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\]
Kyun: \([-2, 2]\) lo aur us mein se sirf \(t = 1\) nikaal do. Isi liye 1 ke paas gol bracket hai.

Step 4: \(x(t)\) ki range
Domain par \(t^{2}\) har value 0 (jab \(t = 0\)) se 4 (jab \(t = \pm 2\)) tak leta hai. Is liye \(4 - t^{2}\) ki range \([0, 4]\) hai, aur us ke square root \(x(t)\) ki range \([0, 2]\).
Kyun: square root barhte hue numbers ko barhta hua hi rakhta hai: \(\sqrt{0} = 0\), \(\sqrt{4} = 2\). \(t = 1\) nikaalne se koi \(x\) value zaaya nahin hoti, kyun ke \(t = -1\) wahi \(x = \sqrt{3}\) de deta hai.

Step 5: \(y(t)\) ki range
Yahan ehtiyaat chahiye: \(t\) sirf domain mein hai, poori real line par nahin. Is liye domain ke dono hisson ko alag dekhte hain:
\[-2 \le t < 1 \Rightarrow -3 \le t - 1 < 0\]
\[\Rightarrow y \le -\tfrac{1}{3}\]
\[1 < t \le 2 \Rightarrow 0 < t - 1 \le 1\]
\[\Rightarrow y \ge 1\]
To \(y(t)\) ki range \((-\infty, -\tfrac{1}{3}] \cup [1, \infty)\) hai.
Kyun: agar \(u\) \([-3, 0)\) mein ho to \(\frac{1}{u} \le -\frac{1}{3}\), aur \(u\) zero ke qareeb jaye to \(\frac{1}{u}\) bohat bara negative ho jata hai; agar \(u\) \((0, 1]\) mein ho to \(\frac{1}{u} \ge 1\).
Dhyan dein: kitab yahan likhti hai ke \(y\) "0 ke ilawa koi bhi real number" ho sakta hai; yeh ghalat hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye). Misal: \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) ke liye \(t = 3\) chahiye, jo domain mein nahin.

Step 6: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ki range
Definition ke mutabiq range output vectors ka set hai, yani curve ke points:
\[\Big\{\Big\langle\sqrt{4 - t^{2}}, \tfrac{1}{t - 1}\Big\rangle\Big\}\]
jahan \(t \in [-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\). Agar \(t\) ko khatam karein (\(t = 1 + \frac{1}{y}\)) to yahi set points \(\big(\sqrt{4 - (1 + \frac{1}{y})^{2}},\ y\big)\) ki shakal mein likha ja sakta hai, jahan \(y \le -\frac{1}{3}\) ya \(y \ge 1\).
Kyun: \(x\) aur \(y\) azaad nahin hain: ek hi \(t\) dono ko tay karta hai. Is liye har \(x\) value ko har \(y\) value ke saath jorna ghalat hai. Kitab ki shart \(x \ne \sqrt{3}\) bhi ghalat hai, kyun ke \(t = -1\) par \(x = \sqrt{3}\) milta hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(t = -1\): \(\mathbf{r}(-1) = \langle\sqrt{3}, -\frac{1}{2}\rangle\); to \(x = \sqrt{3}\) range mein hai.
\(t = -2\): \(\langle 0, -\frac{1}{3}\rangle\); \(t = 0\): \(\langle 2, -1\rangle\); \(t = 2\): \(\langle 0, 1\rangle\): \(y\) ki kinare wali values \(-\frac{1}{3}\) aur \(1\) waqai milti hain.
\(y = \frac{1}{2}\): \(\frac{1}{t - 1} = \frac{1}{2}\) se \(t = 3\), jo domain se bahar hai; is liye koi output \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) nahin deta. Hamara jawab har tarah se durust hai.
blocks.answer: Domain: \(t \in [-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\). Range: domain ke har \(t\) ke liye points \(\big\langle\sqrt{4 - t^{2}}, \frac{1}{t - 1}\big\rangle\) ka set, jahan \(x \in [0, 2]\) aur \(y \in (-\infty, -\frac{1}{3}] \cup [1, \infty)\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Is misaal mein kitab ki do baatein ghalat hain.
1. Kitab likhti hai ke \(y(t)\) "0 ke ilawa koi bhi real number" ho sakta hai. Lekin \(t\) sirf \([-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\) mein hai, is liye \(y(t) = \frac{1}{t-1}\) ki values \((-\infty, -\frac{1}{3}] \cup [1, \infty)\) hain; maslan \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) ke liye \(t = 3\) chahiye.
2. Kitab aakhri range \(\{(x, y) \mid 0 \le x \le 2, y \in \mathbb{R}, y \ne 0, x \ne \sqrt{3}\}\) chhaapti hai. Shart \(x \ne \sqrt{3}\) ghalat hai (\(t = -1\) par \(x = \sqrt{3}\), \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\)), aur tamam pairs ka set bohat bara hai. Sahi range output vectors \(\big\langle\sqrt{4 - t^{2}}, \frac{1}{t-1}\big\rangle\), \(t \in [-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\) ka set hai, yani points \(\big(\sqrt{4 - (1 + \frac{1}{y})^{2}}, y\big)\) jahan \(y \le -\frac{1}{3}\) ya \(y \ge 1\).
Domain \([-2, 1) \cup (1, 2]\) aur \(x(t)\) ki range \([0, 2]\) kitab mein sahi hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: is misaal mein agar \(t = 1.5\) ho to output vector kya hoga? \(x = \sqrt{4 - 2.25} = \sqrt{1.75}\), \(y = \frac{1}{0.5} = 2\). Dekhiye, \(y = 2 \ge 1\), bilkul hamari range ke mutabiq.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal (kitab ka sawal nahin): \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{t + 1}\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{t - 2}\hat{j}\).
Domain: \(\sqrt{t + 1}\) ke liye \(t \ge -1\); \(\frac{1}{t-2}\) ke liye \(t \ne 2\). Intersection: \(t \in [-1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)\).
\(x\) ki range: \(\sqrt{t + 1}\) barhta hua function hai, aur sirf \(t = 2\) nikla hai, jo \(x = \sqrt{3}\) deta. Is dafa koi doosra \(t\) \(\sqrt{3}\) nahin deta, is liye yahan waqai \(x \ne \sqrt{3}\): range \([0, \sqrt{3}) \cup (\sqrt{3}, \infty)\).
\(y\) ki range: \(-1 \le t < 2\) par \(t - 2 \in [-3, 0)\), to \(y \le -\frac{1}{3}\); \(t > 2\) par \(y > 0\). Yani \((-\infty, -\frac{1}{3}] \cup (0, \infty)\).
Sabaq: koi value tabhi nikalti hai jab domain ka koi bhi \(t\) use na de sake. Kitab wali misaal mein \(t = -1\) ne \(\sqrt{3}\) de diya tha; is misaal mein koi nahin deta. Har dafa check karna parta hai.

Range nikaalne ka ek aasan tareeqa yaad kar lijiye. Pehle domain ko hisson (pieces) mein likhiye. Phir har hisse par har component ko alag dekhiye: woh kahan se shuru hota hai, kahan khatam, aur beech mein barhta hai ya ghatta hai. Kinare (end points) aur \(t = 0\) jaisi aasan values rakh kar dekhiye. Aakhir mein yaad rakhiye ke vector function ki range asal mein points ka set (curve) hai; components ki ranges sirf yeh batati hain ke curve kahan tak phaila hua hai.

Ek chhoti si baat number line ke brackets ke baare mein bhi: square bracket \([\ ]\) ka matlab hai woh number shaamil hai, gol bracket \((\ )\) ka matlab shaamil nahin. \([-2, 1)\) mein \(-2\) shaamil hai (kyun ke \(\sqrt{0} = 0\) theek hai) magar \(1\) nahin (kyun ke wahan denominator zero hai). Exam mein in brackets ki ghalti par bhi marks katte hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: kitab wali misaal mein \(t = 1\) ke bilkul qareeb, maslan \(t = 0.99\) aur \(t = 1.01\), par \(y\) kya hoga? \(t = 0.99\) par \(y = \frac{1}{-0.01} = -100\), aur \(t = 1.01\) par \(y = 100\). Yani \(t = 1\) ke dono taraf curve bohat neeche aur bohat upar chala jata hai. Isi liye \(y\) ki range mein \(-\infty\) aur \(\infty\) dono aate hain, magar beech ki values \((-\frac{1}{3}, 1)\) kabhi nahin aatin.

Aakhir mein ek ustad wala mashwara: domain aur range ke sawal mein jawab hamesha saaf hisson mein likhiye. Pehle "Domain:" likh kar interval, phir "Range of x(t):", phir "Range of y(t):", aur aakhir mein poori range. Is tarah examiner ko aap ki soch ka har qadam nazar aata hai, aur agar kahin chhoti si ghalti ho bhi jaye to baqi qadmon ke marks mil jate hain. Aur jab bhi kisi value ko range se nikaalein, ek lamha ruk kar poochiye: kya domain ka koi aur \(t\) yeh value de sakta hai?

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Step-1: har component ka domain alag nikaalo. Step-2: \(\mathbf{r}\) ka domain un sab ka intersection hai.
2. Range = domain ke har \(t\) par bane output vectors \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka set, yani curve ke points.
3. Component ki range nikaalte waqt sirf domain wale \(t\) lo, hisson mein baant kar.
4. Jawab ko \(t\) ki kuch values (kinare, \(t = 0\)) rakh kar check karo.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Component ki range poori real line par nikaal lena, domain ko bhool kar (isi se "\(y\) zero ke ilawa sab kuch" wali ghalti banti hai).
2. Components ki ranges ko azaad samajh kar range ko tamam pairs \((x, y)\) likh dena.
3. Baghair check kiye values nikaal dena: \(x = \sqrt{3}\) to \(t = -1\) par milta hai.
4. \([-2, 2]\) mein se \(t = 1\) nikaalna bhool jana.
